quotes.text: checking that families have been correctly assigned within households by referring to the relationship grid

The harmonised definition of the household response unit is “one person living alone or a group of people (not necessarily related) living at the same address who share cooking facilities and share a living room or sitting room or dining area. The LFS definition differs slightly. The LFS adds students who live in halls of residence in term-time and residents in National Health Service accommodation to the coverage allowed in the harmonised definition, but these are clearly identified and the harmonised definition can be derived.
Family:      DVs created for each family on the database; on a flat file each family member would carry the same value for each family based DV;
The following primary topics are not included on the LFS : Agency workers, Carers and Mobile Phone use.

assessments.reasoning: Regarding member_to_member_relationships: Section 6.3 refers to a 'relationship grid' and Table 15.1 lists 'Relationship to HRP', but the text does not state that relationships are recorded member-to-member (matrix/pointer) rather than relative to the household head/HRP. Regarding extended_ties: While 'Relationship to HRP' is collected, the text does not detail response categories to confirm extended ties (e.g., grandparents, siblings, non-kin, same-sex partners). Regarding multiple_household_criteria: Section 15 Note (i) explicitly details the criteria for defining/separating household units (sharing cooking facilities and a living/dining room, plus specific additions for students and NHS residents). Regarding sub-units: Section 6.2 and 6.3 confirm that family sub-units within households are identified and assigned family-level derived variables. Regarding caregiving_relationships: Section 15 explicitly states that 'Carers' are not included on the LFS.
